title: SIG.encode does not run under no_grad despite its docstring, and the encoder is in the optimizer's param groups, so any caller's backward trains it
failure: SIG_MODE=learned (the default arm). The body has no torch.no_grad() anywhere: :186 returns `st.encoder(units.to(...))`, which builds an autograd graph through _Encoder.emb and _Encoder.proj. compose.py:1985-1987 puts those very parameters into the optimizer: `opt_api.build(opt, param_groups={..., "encoder": list(sig_api.encoder_parameters(sig, sysm.sig))}, ...)`. So whenever the loop computes a signature for routing and later calls backward on the LM/FAB loss, encoder gradients accumulate and the next optimizer step applies them -- the signature encoder is trained by a loss that is not its contrastive objective, while sig.train_steps (:144) counts only SIG.train_step. The same path lets an instrument that calls encode() inside a graph move the encoder, which is the exact thing the docstring promises it cannot do.
evidence: Docstring :155-156: 'Runs under no_grad and never touches the optimizer, so an instrument calling it cannot move the encoder (the G7 digest holds across it).' Body :164-186 contains no `torch.no_grad()` and no `.detach()`; contrast sig/api.py:46 and :128, where build() does wrap its draws in `with torch.no_grad():`.
fix: Wrap the whole computation: `with torch.no_grad():` around :177-186 (both the bigram and learned arms), returning a detached tensor. If some future caller genuinely needs a differentiable signature, that has to be a separate declared entry point, because this one's contract is that it cannot move the encoder.
_triage_evidence: sig/api.py's encode() body (lines 167-189) still has no torch.no_grad() anywhere. Ran it: v = SIG.encode(cfg, st, windows) has requires_grad=True and a live grad_fn; v.sum().backward() populates st.encoder.emb.weight.grad (not None).

title: SIG.encode does not run under no_grad, so an instrument that calls it can move the encoder
failure: Ran it: `v = SIG.encode(cfg, st, windows)` returns `requires_grad=True` with a grad_fn, and `v.sum().backward()` leaves a non-None `st.encoder.emb.weight.grad`. Any diagnostic, probe or eval path that calls encode and backwards through the value it produced accumulates gradients into the signature encoder -- and since the encoder is in OPT's "encoder" param group, the next optimizer step applies them. That is the class of defect spine/rng.py's frozen_rng exists for ("diagnostics were silently editing runs"), reaching the router's only input.
evidence: Docstring: "Runs under no_grad and never touches the optimizer, so an instrument calling it cannot move the encoder (the G7 digest holds across it)." The body has no `torch.no_grad()` anywhere; line 187 is a bare `return st.encoder(units.to(...))`. Training has its own entry points (SIG.train_step, SIG.warm_up), so no_grad here costs nothing.
fix: Wrap the whole body after the shape refusal in `with torch.no_grad():` on both arms (the bigram arm's `index_add_` too).
_triage_evidence: Duplicate of the other SIG no_grad finding; confirmed by the same backward() test (grad populated on st.encoder.emb.weight).

title: The bigram arm returns an all-zero signature whenever width_units < 2, which is exactly the zero vector the contract says it may never return.
failure: At SIG_MODE=bigram with width_units=1 (reachable at LM_CTX=1, which LM.resolve accepts, and accepted by SIG.build which only refuses width < 1), `units[:, :-1]` is empty, so `idx` has shape (N, 0), `v.index_add_` adds nothing, and `v / v.norm(...).clamp_min(1e-8)` returns exact zeros. Verified: `S.encode(cfg_bigram, st_width1, torch.randint(0,256,(4,1)))` -> a (4, 8) tensor of all 0.0, no exception. Every window then has an identical (zero) signature: FAB's routing cosine is identical for every expert, DOM's boundary test can never fire, every centroid is the zero vector, and nothing anywhere fails -- the precise C4/C5 failure mode this function was written to make impossible.
evidence: sig/api.py:182-186 `idx = ((units[:, :-1] * 31 + units[:, 1:]) % st.encoder.shape[0]).long()` ... `return v / v.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)`. Contract contradicted, in the same function's docstring: "a caller that cannot supply width_units units gets an EXCEPTION, never a narrower window and never a zero vector. This is the whole of the C4/C5 repair." (sig/api.py:152-154). The learned arm has no such hole -- at width_units=1 it still returns unit vectors.
fix: Refuse in SIG.build when `mode == "bigram" and width < 2`, naming SIG_MODE, SIG_WIDTH_UNITS and both numbers (a bigram encoder needs at least two units), rather than emitting a well-formed zero vector.
_triage_evidence: SIG.build has no `mode=="bigram" and width<2` refusal (only a blanket `width<1` check at sig/api.py:112-117), and encode()'s bigram branch (lines 181-188) is unchanged. Ran it: SIG.build(mode=bigram, width_units=1, ...) then encode() on a (4,1) batch returns a (4,8) tensor that is exactly all zeros.

title: sig.encode_calls is incremented by the number of windows, so the ledger's 'calls' counter holds the 'windows' quantity and sig.encode_windows does not exist at all.
failure: The contract declares two distinct counters: `sig.encode_calls` and `sig.encode_windows`. The body has only the first and adds the window count to it. Verified: after `SIG.build(...)` (`counters['sig.encode_calls'] == 0`) and ONE call `S.encode(cfg, st, torch.randint(0,256,(4,16)))`, `st.counters['sig.encode_calls'] == 4`. A report reading that row prints 4 encoder calls for 1 call, and the two quantities the contract wants separated -- how often the encoder was invoked vs how many windows were characterised -- collapse into one number that is neither's label.
evidence: sig/api.py:178 `st.counters["sig.encode_calls"] += int(units.shape[0])`; the dict built at sig/api.py:141-144 contains `"sig.encode_calls": 0` and no `sig.encode_windows` key. Contract: "DID IT FIRE: sig.encode_calls, sig.encode_windows, and sig.encode_width_seen asserted equal to st.width_units on EVERY call" (sig/api.py:161-163).
fix: `st.counters["sig.encode_calls"] += 1` and `st.counters["sig.encode_windows"] += int(units.shape[0])`, seeding both keys in build().
_triage_evidence: sig/api.py:180 is unchanged: `st.counters["sig.encode_calls"] += int(units.shape[0])`. build()'s counters dict (lines 143-146) still has no `sig.encode_windows` key. Ran it: one encode() call on a batch of 4 windows leaves sig.encode_calls == 4.

title: encode adds the WINDOW count to sig.encode_calls and never produces sig.encode_windows, so the two documented counters collapse into one wrong number
failure: `st.counters["sig.encode_calls"] += int(units.shape[0])` adds N, not 1. Ran it: one call encoding 4 windows leaves `sig.encode_calls: 4`. The counters dict built in build() has no `sig.encode_windows` key, and SIG.counters(sig, st) is the only channel out, so the windows figure does not exist and the calls figure is really the windows figure. A reader computing windows-per-call, or checking that the encoder was queried once per flush, gets a number the run did not produce.
evidence: Docstring: "DID IT FIRE: sig.encode_calls, sig.encode_windows, and sig.encode_width_seen asserted equal to st.width_units on EVERY call". build() line 144 initialises `"sig.encode_calls": 0, "sig.train_steps": 0` and nothing else. Also: encode's "LEVERS READ: mode, d, bigram_dim" names three levers the body never reads (it reads st.mode, st.d and st.encoder.shape[0]), which is what lets K4 report them declared-and-read on prose alone.
fix: `counters["sig.encode_calls"] += 1` and `counters["sig.encode_windows"] += int(units.shape[0])`, initialising both in build(); record sig.encode_width_seen and correct encode's LEVERS READ line to "none directly -- everything comes off SigState".
_triage_evidence: Duplicate of the sig.encode_calls findings above; same unchanged code, same test result (encode_calls==4 after one 4-window call, no encode_windows key).
